page.title: Philosophical Keywords
page.subtitle: Core Epicurean concepts and imagery in the proem of Book III of De rerum natura

keywords.name: lumen
paragraphs: The light of Epicurean truth and scientific clarity (<foreign>clarum extollere lumen</foreign>). Lucretius places this metaphor at the opening of Book III in direct opposition to human ignorance and terror (<foreign>tenebris tantis</foreign>).
The image returns in line 22 (<foreign>large diffuso lumine ridet</foreign>), where radiant light illuminates the tranquil dwellings of the gods (<foreign>sedesque quietae</foreign>).

keywords.name: ratio
paragraphs: The rational system and natural philosophy established by Epicurus. Born of a godlike intellect (<foreign>divina mente coorta</foreign>), this doctrine proclaims the ultimate truths of physics, dispersing the irrational terrors of the soul.

keywords.name: moenia mundi
paragraphs: The ramparts or outer boundary walls of the visible universe. Upon the revelation of Epicurean doctrine, these cosmological boundaries give way (<foreign>discedunt</foreign>), allowing the philosopher's intellect to behold infinite cosmic space.

keywords.name: inane
paragraphs: The infinite void: one of the two foundational constituents of Epicurean physics alongside material atoms (<foreign>corpora</foreign>). An intangible space devoid of resistance across which all atomic events and movements take place (<foreign>totum video per inane geri res</foreign>).
